title: Subtoken ID shift — canary debugging walkthrough
content:
SUMMARY:
Short: During a canary rollout of model v2024-11-13, we observed decoding errors and semantic regressions traced back to a subtoken ID shift introduced by an updated tokenizer artifact. Canary traffic (5%) experienced higher model perplexity, increased tokenization-mismatch errors in the preprocessor, and several downstream reranker failures. Immediate mitigation: rollback canary to v2024-10-30, force-served previous tokenizer mapping, and open this incident review + runbook draft.

IMPACT:
- Affected customers: small percentage of hosted-api requests routed to canary instances (~5% of production).
- Observable user impact: increased hallucinations and some truncated outputs for prompts that include special tokens (code snippets, user mentions). No PII leakage, no data loss.
- Metrics: tokenization-mismatch log rate spiked from ~0.2/min to 18/min (observed across 03:12–03:41 UTC). Average response latency increased by ~120ms on canary hosts. Model perplexity on sampled prompts rose by ~22%.

DETECTION SIGNALS:
- Alert: "tokenization-mismatch-rate" fired at 03:14 UTC (threshold 5/m).
- Canary SLO dashboard showed increased perplexity and higher error budget burn.
- Oncall pager (sms + slack) from automated canary checks (smoke-eval) flagged a >15% regression in semantic-similarity eval.

TIMELINE (UTC):
- 02:50 — CI/CD pipeline pushed model v2024-11-13 image to canary pool (rolling 5% traffic). Tokenizer artifact v1.8.0 also deployed as part of image bundle.
- 03:05 — First anomalous requests seen in canary logs (decoding warnings).
- 03:12 — Monitoring alert triggered for tokenization-mismatch-rate.
- 03:18 — Oncall SRE (Samira) started investigation, confirmed mismatched token ids in canary vs prod tokenizer for test inputs.
- 03:25 — Canary rollback to v2024-10-30 initiated via orchestrator rollback job; traffic moved off canary hosts.
- 03:35 — Forced tokenizer mapping override applied to canary hosts to ensure consistent token->id mapping until full fix.
- 03:42 — Alerts cleared; extra smoke-eval run passed for rollback image.
- 04:30 — Postmortem triage meeting scheduled and follow-ups assigned.

ROOT CAUSE (high level):
A tokenizer rebuild process changed the serialized vocabulary ordering. The model weights were trained with the previous tokenizer mapping (v1.7.x) but the release packaging step referenced the latest tokenizer artifact (v1.8.0) without checking compatibility. Two contributing issues: (1) ambiguous tokenizer artifact naming (no content hash pinned in model metadata), and (2) rollout pipeline lacked a token-alignment smoke test. The mismatch manifested as a systematic "subtoken id shift" for ~3% of commonly used subtokens (special tokens and some frequent punctuation), leading to incorrect embeddings and decoding behavior.

TECHNICAL DETAILS:
- What happened: v1.8.0 tokenizer introduced a new special token ordering and regenerated BPE merges using a different merge-priority seed in the tokenizer build. This caused certain tokens to receive different integer ids (an offset for ~114 subtokens). The model expects ids from v1.7.x; feeding tokens with shifted ids results in embedding lookups pointing to unrelated vectors.
- Packaging bug: release pipeline step 'bundle_model_assets' picks latest tokenizer from /artifacts/tokenizers/latest rather than the tokenizer id recorded in the model's metadata file (model_manifest.json). The model_manifest contained the tokenizer name but not an immutable content hash.
- Why not caught earlier: unit tests validated from-text encoding/decoding roundtrip for the tokenizer alone but not cross-checked tokenizer->model embedding alignment. Canary smoke-eval used semantic tests but not token-id fingerprinting.

COMMANDS / QUICK REPRO STEPS USED DURING ONCALL:
- Dump token ids for a canonical input against both tokenizers:
  python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t_old=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer-v1.7.json'); t_new=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer-v1.8.json'); s='def hello(): return 42'; print(t_old.encode(s).ids); print(t_new.encode(s).ids)"
- Check id differences count:
  python - <<'PY'
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t1=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer-v1.7.json')
t2=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer-v1.8.json')
count=0
for tok in ['<pad>','<bos>','<eos>','<sep>','def','return','(' ,')',':',' indentation']:
    i1=t1.token_to_id(tok)
    i2=t2.token_to_id(tok)
    if i1!=i2:
        print(tok,i1,i2)
        count+=1
print('diffs',count)
PY
- Hash vocab files to assert identity: sha256 tokenizer-v1.7.json tokenizer-v1.8.json

MITIGATION / SHORT-TERM FIXES APPLIED:
- Immediate rollback: Canary image rolled back to v2024-10-30 (completed 03:25 UTC).
- Forced mapping: For environments where rollback was delayed, applied an override mapping layer that translates new tokenizer ids back to expected ids for the model (temporary shim).
- Artifact quarantine: quarantined tokenizer v1.8.0 in artifact registry and added a manual approval flag.
- Hotfix PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1273 implemented model_manifest validation and asserts hash equality between model's declared tokenizer and bundled tokenizer.

LONG-TERM FIXES / RUNBOOK ADDITIONS (proposed):
1) Tokenizer-to-model fingerprinting
   - Require tokenizer artifact content hash in model_manifest.json and validate at bundle/publish time.
   - Prevent 'latest' fallback; bundler must error if manifest hash mismatch.
   Owner: Jinwoo — due 2024-11-22.
2) Token alignment smoke test in rollout pipeline
   - Run a fast check comparing token ids for a set of canonical inputs between model-declared tokenizer and bundled tokenizer. Fail rollout if any mismatch above threshold.
   Owner: Ariel — due 2024-11-20.
3) Canary smoke eval augmentation
   - Add token-id drift metric to canary dashboards and set alert thresholds.
   Owner: eng-sre — due 2024-11-21.
4) Artifact naming and immutability policy
   - Enforce content-hash-based artifact naming; registry should reject ambiguous names.
   Owner: infra-release — due 2024-12-01.
5) Post-deploy verification job
   - Short-lived job after each rollout that validates end-to-end tokenization -> embedding indices on a sampled prompt set.
   Owner: platform-engineering — due 2024-11-28.

RUNBOOK (draft steps for oncall):
- If tokenization-mismatch-rate alert fires:
  1) Identify affected host group and canary percentage.
  2) Run token-id diff script against model_manifest declared tokenizer and the tokenizer file bundled on host.
  3) If mismatch confirmed and canary <10%: pause rollout (set canary-percentage=0) and rollback to previous model image.
  4) If rollback not immediately possible, apply tokenizer-id-translation shim (see scripts/shims/id_translate.py) as temporary mitigation.
  5) Open incident ticket and notify owners; escalate to release-engineering if packaging mismatch.

LESSONS LEARNED:
- Even small tokenizer id shifts can have outsized semantic impact because the model relies on exact id->embedding alignment.
- Artifact immutability and explicit pinning are essential — "latest" pointers are dangerous for model-serving artifacts.
- Canary smoke evals must include low-level compatibility checks (token-id hashes) in addition to higher-level semantic tests.

ATTACHMENTS & EXAMPLE LOGS (snippets):
- Sample log line that alerted:
  2024-11-15T03:13:58Z ERROR preprocessor: tokenization_mismatch input_id=abc123 expected_token_id=457 actual=789 path=/v1/generate request_id=...
- Token-id diff excerpt:
  '<bos>'  -> prod 1 vs canary 5
  'def'    -> prod 245 vs canary 101
  'return' -> prod 423 vs canary 420
  diffs total: 114 subtokens

FOLLOW-UPS (owners):
- Implement manifest hash checks: Jinwoo (in PR #1273) — ETA 2024-11-22.
- Add token-alignment smoke test: Ariel — ETA 2024-11-20.
- Update runbook and canary dashboards: Samira & eng-sre — ETA 2024-11-21.
- Audit tokenizers in artifact registry and quarantine ambiguous names: infra-release — ETA 2024-12-01.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DISCUSSION POINTS:
- Do we want token-id translation shims to be a supported temporary mitigation or treated as emergency-only hack?
- Should we change training infra to store tokenizer hash in model checkpoints automatically?
- How to best version specialized/special-token ordering when tokenizer rebuilds are necessary (semantic-preserving merges)?

NOTES TO SELF / ONCALL HINTS:
- When investigating, always compare both the tokenizer json and the model_manifest.json content-hash.
- Prefer a small canonical prompt set to quickly compute id diffs (keeps smoke eval < 30s).
- Slack thread: #inc-SRE-4821 contains real-time debugging snippets and traces.

END.
